newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures close sharply lower.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures closed sharply lower, with declines in the U.S. bond market inspiring a strong selloff in the Standard & Poor's 500 pit, traders and analysts said.
"We were quiet until about one o'clock," one S&P futures trader said about June S&P's sudden descent from 835.50 to 830.60 within 15 minutes.

The plunge accompanied the selloff in the U.S. bond market where June T-bond futures fell to 109-27/32, S&P floor traders noted. Several funds were large sellers, helping touch off sell-stop orders from 833.00 to 830.60.
One fund alone sold 1,000 contracts after a major U.S. dealer had steadily sold about 1,000 June starting around midday, traders said.
June S&Ps found light short-covering bids at 830.60, which kept the contract from falling to the 15-point initial daily limit at 829.75.
The pre-closing imbalances were on the sell side as some May options on futures went into expiration. The imbalances before the opening were also on the sell side.
Most traders and analysts said the theme of the day was the market's overbought condition, especially since June S&Ps set an all-time high at 846.50 late Thursday.
The all-time high was only slightly above the contract's previous record high of 846.30 and formed a double-top on the charts, according to one technical analyst.
"We got ahead of ourselves yesterday and now we are seeing the after-effects," he said.
June fell through the two-week trendline support level of 836.50.

In addition, pressure from Hewlett-Packard Co stock spilled into technology-rich Nasdaq stocks and subsequently dragged down S&Ps. Hewlett-Packard reported quarterly earnings well below Wall Street forecasts.
Fears that falling computer-related stocks would lead investors out of U.S. stocks were exacerbated by the rise in the U.S. long bond yield.
AMG Data Services, based in Arcata, Calif., said cash flows into U.S. equity funds fell sharply for the week ended Thursday, as investors shifted money into fixed-income funds.
Jitters that the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday will result in a 25-basis-point U.S. rate hike lifted U.S. bond yields and weighed on bond prices.
Fair value for June S&Ps remained at 3.10 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 4.50 points and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 2.30 points.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were off 12.70 at 832.05, NYSE Composites were off 4.25 at 434.80, KCBT Value Lines were down 4.60 at 733.30, Nikkeis were up 220 at 20,225, Midcap 400s were off 1.15 at 270.25, Russell 2000s were down 0.30 at 366.75, and Nasdaq 100s fell 13.25 to 920.25. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
